compare: world and installed DB plus scripts/triggers
cases.stimulus: In one original APK transaction, install names jq and curl from the declared signed offline repositories into a fresh qualified Alpine environment. Resolve dependency versions through unchanged APK.

cases.scope: No HTTPS/network qualification from the curl local-file case.
cases.stimulus: Run installed jq against pinned JSON including a regex operation requiring oniguruma; run installed curl against a pinned local file using its original file transport. Record exact argv/stdin/output/status.

cases.scope: Non-vacuous trigger effect only; not qualification of every script or trigger path.
cases.stimulus: On paired fresh private states only, remove the baseline /usr/bin/yes symlink after recording its exact original target. Install jq/curl with unchanged APK, BusyBox and its original registered trigger. Verify original trigger executes and restores the exact link and program behavior; Linux establishes the expected result first.
Install an older genuine signed version, select a later declared signed snapshot/version through original APK, execute new payload, compare DB/metadata/scripts/config handling, and restart.
Use original APK to remove selected installed roots; compare original dependency cleanup, world/DB/payload and script effects, then restart and query both retained and removed state.

cases.scope: Normal restart is not power-loss consistency; crash gates must be separately specified.
cases.stimulus: After successful install and after upgrade/remove, perform the declared durable commit then restart the single-system candidate and matched Linux reference from their own resulting state. Re-run installed programs and original DB queries.
Use an isolated keyset with the actual repository signer absent or replaced by a declared unrelated public key. Original signature policy remains enabled.
Modify a private copy of a signed index without resigning; retain the mutation and format validity. Compare the original authentication failure, not merely a decompression parse failure.
Modify a private copy of a selected authentic APK without resigning, retaining parseability and exact mutation record. Compare original verification failure and resulting state.

cases.scope: Repository availability failure, not dependency-resolver conflict proof.
cases.stimulus: Remove an archive required by the unmodified signed index from a private no-network repository copy.

Choose a manifest-declared unsatisfiable request or a genuine package whose required dependency is absent from the declared authenticated repository set. Record original resolver rejection and state effects.

cases.scope: An invented missing version does not establish a genuine conflict case.
cases.stimulus: Use genuine authenticated incompatible packages/providers that cannot coexist in the requested original APK transaction. Preserve original policy and selection decisions.
Use a declared genuine wrong-architecture input through the normal original manager path and compare the original rejection/selection behavior.

fixed_reference.invocation: direct original apk; exact complete argv to be pinned against declared runtime

prerequisites: Complete source/build/dependency/helper provenance or explicitly separated supplied-original-binary ABI profile
Protected native application startup, Linux ABI and common writable filesystem semantics
Real manager-specific namespace/runtime/database ownership, not descriptor labels
Two-version signed upgrade pair and genuine conflict fixtures
Offline repository config, absent/stale cache rules and original signature checks pinned identically
Observable original script/trigger effects and durable commit/restart

result_rules.negative_failures: Compare original exit class/status, diagnostics and actual DB/filesystem/script effects; do not assume failure is side-effect-free.
result_rules.normalization: Keep raw bytes and allow only explicitly declared nondeterministic fields; never normalize package decisions, scripts, payload or trust outcomes.
result_rules.performance: Separate all-system matched measurements; no efficiency conclusion until both comparable systems exist.
